topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Rachel Liu (Harmony CTO), Marcus Chen (ML Eng), Aisha Patel (Security)

00:00 - Ethan Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm ethan from redwood inference, with maya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
00:06 - Rachel Liu: good thanks, just joined from SF, morning for us, afternoon for you.
00:10 - Maya Singh: great, i'll share my screen and we'll jump into the model catalog demo. quick agenda: filter by task, show perf/bench stats, compatibility matrix, then q&a. sound good?
00:20 - Marcus Chen: sounds good, high level — our big goals are latency for chat, cost for embeddings across search, and data residency.
00:28 - Ethan Park: perfect. quick qual: what are you running now? cloud infra? open-source models?
00:33 - Rachel Liu: currently we host an in-house LLM stack on GCP, mixed models — some tuned Mistral variants and a few llama forks, but maintenance is getting heavy. we're looking to either move to hosted or dedicated offload.
00:45 - Marcus Chen: also, context lengths matter — some workflows hit 8k and a few go to 16k for long patient notes.
00:53 - Aisha Patel: security: we need KMS for keys, SOC 2 evidence, and audit logs that we can ingest into our SIEM.
01:02 - Maya Singh: got it. i'll show the catalog UI, the filters include task (chat/generation/embeddings), model family, size, latency bracket, cost-per-token estimate, and compatibility tags (quantization-friendly, 8k/16k tested, streaming support).
01:20 - Maya Singh: (screen) here we have a list — Llama2-13b, Mistral-7b, RedMistral-tuned, Mixtral, GPT-NeoX-20b community weights, and some curated smaller models for embeddings. you can toggle '8k tested' and 'quantization friendly' to narrow down.
01:40 - Marcus Chen: can you show how benchmarks are surfaced? we need numbers, not just badges.
01:44 - Maya Singh: yes — clicking a model opens the detail pane: we show median latency p50/p95 for typical 256/1024 inputs, tokens/sec throughput, GPU memory footprint, and a notes field showing optimal quantization (e.g., q4f16) and kernel hints. there's also a downloadable CSV with run configs.
02:05 - Ethan Park: for your use-case, marcus, we pre-run bench suites across sequence lengths — 512, 2k, 8k, 16k — and across instance types (A100, H100, and cheaper T4-like).
02:16 - Rachel Liu: do you publish the exact infra used for the numbers? we need reproducibility.
02:19 - Maya Singh: yes, each benchmark row includes hardware, batch size, sequence length, compiler flags (if any), and the runtime version. we also include notes about tokenizer differences and any KV cache changes.
02:32 - Marcus Chen: what about quantized variants? we need to understand quality delta vs latency/cost.
02:36 - Maya Singh: the catalog states recommended quantization level and a delta estimate — e.g., Mistral-7b q4f16 shows ~1.2% rouge drop on our web eval prompts, while latency improved 2.3x. we link to eval sets and you can download the prompt set used.
02:51 - Aisha Patel: curious about compatibility matrix for private deployment — like which models are allowed on our VPC hardware and any licensing constraints.
02:58 - Ethan Park: good question. the compatibility matrix is a separate tab; it maps models to supported runtime variants and notes on licensing (e.g., community vs permissive). for private/VPC we'll surface any model license flags and whether we can bundle them with Private offering.
03:15 - Marcus Chen: can you demo filtering for low-latency chat models? we need p95 < 250ms on token generation ideally.
03:20 - Maya Singh: sure. (filters) set latency target p95 < 250ms, task=chat, and region=us-west. results: a few candidates: Llama2-13b optimized xformers build on H100, Red-optimized Mistral-7b q4f16 on A100, and a trimmed GPT-NeoX variant. each has an estimated cost-per-1k tokens and expected throughput.
03:42 - Ethan Park: important nuance — we show per-token cost at different batch sizes and also show the routing policy option: you can route low-latency requests to dedicated pool and fallback to hosted cheaper pool for background workloads.
03:55 - Rachel Liu: routing policy sounds useful. can it be per-route? like we want chat route pinned to dedicated, embeddings route on hosted.
04:02 - Maya Singh: yes per-route routing. console has a route config: model selection, fallback model family, region, and capacity tier. you can also attach SLOs that will trigger fallback automatically.
04:14 - Marcus Chen: how do you handle streaming with long context? kv cache across requests?
04:18 - Maya Singh: runtime maintains KV cache per session; for streaming we keep low-latency first-token paths and incrementally load KV pages. for very long contexts we recommend chunking plus prefix caching; the console shows cache hit rates and estimated cost savings.
04:33 - Ethan Park: we also do automatic prefix caching for common system prompts which often reduces token regen.
04:38 - Rachel Liu: benchmark transparency again — if we run our prompt set, can you run a joint benchmark?
04:42 - Maya Singh: absolutely. typical POC flow: you share prompt set and expected qps, we run in our dedicated env replicating your infra target, and share full CSV + raw logs.
04:53 - Marcus Chen: for embeddings at scale — our search index uses 128-dim vectors and we do 50k queries/day. how do you price embeddings?
04:59 - Ethan Park: hosted is usage-based per-embedding unit; we show estimated monthly cost in the console when you simulate traffic. Dedicated gives predictable throughput for a monthly reserved footprint. there's also caching options for repeated queries to reduce cost.
05:14 - Aisha Patel: KMS integration — we need a bring-your-own-KMS option for Private. do you support HSM-backed keys?
05:20 - Maya Singh: yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS, HSM options on-prem, and we have an integration guide. for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping in enterprise plans.
05:33 - Ethan Park: i'll add links to the KMS and SOC 2 docs in the notes.
05:38 - Rachel Liu: one more on model drift/quality monitoring — how do you surface regressions or evaluate rollouts?
05:44 - Maya Singh: Redwood Optimize includes eval suites tied to prompt sets. we run canary rollouts and monitor quality metrics — rouge/bleu or custom metrics — and can auto rollback if quality drops beyond a threshold. you can attach test prompts per route.
05:59 - Marcus Chen: what's the typical delta when moving a model from hosted to dedicated? any perf uplift?
06:03 - Ethan Park: dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and tuned schedulers, so latency/SLOs are more predictable; you may see improved p95 by ~10-30% depending on contention in hosted pools. exact numbers depend on batch sizes and kernel paths.
06:16 - Maya Singh: i'll show the compatibility matrix now — (screen) columns: model, runtime variant, quantization support, max tested seq len, recommended GPU, notes/licensing. filtering shows only '16k tested' models. we have Red-13b-long which explicitly supports 16k with custom chunking and KV improvements.
06:36 - Rachel Liu: can we get the raw compatibility matrix CSV? we'll share it with infra/security.
06:40 - Ethan Park: yes we'll send CSV and a short mapping doc explaining the columns.
06:44 - Marcus Chen: any caveats on tokenizer tokenization differences across models? we saw weird shifts in token counts for med notes.
06:50 - Maya Singh: great point. catalog includes median tokens-per-doc for typical doc shapes. we also run a tokenization profiler and show delta vs a reference tokenizer. for clinical notes we recommend running the profiler during POC.
07:05 - Aisha Patel: licensing — any concerns running some community models in enterprise? we need to ensure license compliance.
07:11 - Ethan Park: the model detail includes license flags; for models with restrictive clauses we flag them and recommend alternatives. for Private we can also remove certain model binaries from the catalog if you request.
07:25 - Rachel Liu: okay, can you walk through the pricing model quickly?
07:29 - Ethan Park: hosted: pay per token/embedding; Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity with a commit, includes autoscale burst options; Private: licensing + support fee plus optional reserved infra. we'll provide a tailored pricing sheet.
07:45 - Maya Singh: quick detour — demo of API snippets. (screen) SDK shows generation call, streaming example, function/tool-calling format, and embeddings endpoint. sample code uses python and node. there is also a console playground to test models live.
07:59 - Marcus Chen: for embeddings latency, do you guarantee p99s?
08:03 - Ethan Park: for hosted we publish typical p50/p95; p99 is harder but for enterprise/dedicated we can include p99 SLOs in the contract.
08:12 - Rachel Liu: thought: for search we'd like embeddings computed in-region to meet residency. do you support region pinning?
08:17 - Maya Singh: yes region pinning per-route; for Private you of course control the region.
08:22 - Marcus Chen: could you elaborate on fallback policies — for example, if the dedicated pool is saturated do you spill over to hosted and how do you handle PII concerns?
08:30 - Maya Singh: policy options include: fail open to hosted, fail closed, or queue. for PII-sensitive routes you can mark them as fail-closed and route only to Private or Dedicated with data controls. the console flags routes with PII policies and prevents accidental fallbacks.
08:46 - Ethan Park: we'll include an example policy template for gradations of sensitivity.
08:50 - Rachel Liu: demo looks good. any notes on running evals longitudinally? we need regression alerts over time.
08:56 - Maya Singh: Optimize runs periodic evals against the baseline; alerts can be emailed or sent to slack/webhook. you can also pin a baseline model and get drift reports.
09:06 - Marcus Chen: for the POC we want: run our prompt set across 3 candidate models, capture latency and quality metrics, and get a recommended configuration (quantization and instance type).
09:13 - Ethan Park: that's doable — typical POC is 2-4 weeks: initial bench + quality check, then a week of production-like traffic if you want.
09:21 - Rachel Liu: timeline — we're aiming to launch a pilot mid-may. so a POC in early april fits.
09:26 - Aisha Patel: security will need to review SOC 2 evidence and KMS integration guide before we sign any contract.
09:32 - Ethan Park: understood, we'll push those docs. i'll own the doc share.
09:36 - Maya Singh: i'm making a quick note — for Marcus: collect prompt set and peak qps. for Aisha: any additional compliance checklist items?
09:42 - Aisha Patel: SAML/SSO integration details, data retention policy, and support for tenant-level audit logs.
09:50 - Maya Singh: all in scope.
09:53 - Ethan Park: okay, recap and next steps: we'll send model catalog deck, compatibility CSV, and benchmarks spreadsheet; schedule POC kickoff week of Apr 6; share SOC2/KMS and SSO docs; Maya will prepare perf configs for 8k/16k. anyone disagree?
10:12 - Rachel Liu: that looks right. one ask — please include cost estimates for embeddings at 50k queries/day.
10:18 - Ethan Park: will do.
10:21 - Marcus Chen: last quick Q — any third-party monitoring integrations? Datadog, prometheus?
10:26 - Maya Singh: yes, console supports exporters and we provide tracing hooks and an OTLP-compatible agent; Datadog dashboards are available as a template.
10:34 - Aisha Patel: thanks all. we'll review and expect the doc pack.
10:37 - Ethan Park: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with an email and attach the files.
10:42 - (call ends)

Notes: transcript has occasional ASR errors in proper nouns — 'Red-optimized' sometimes transcribed as 'redoptimize' in raw logs. We also referenced internal model name 'Red-13b-long' which is a Redwood-verified variant.
